items.title: The S&P 500 and the Dow enter a correction as the Nasdaq falls 5.3% in the AI selloff
items.summary: Nvidia fell 14% and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026, a day after Anthropic's market debut.
items.content_html:

  • 3.70% the S&P 500's fall on Nov 20, to 6,910.42. It and the Dow, down 1.93%, closed more than 10% below their records, a correction

items.title: Citi and PNC join banks making customers liable for what AI agents do with their logins
items.summary: Customers who give outside agents their logins carry the risk, even after a hack. ChatGPT Wallet pays with a network token instead.
items.content_html:
Customers who give outside agents their logins carry the risk, even after a hack. ChatGPT Wallet pays with a network token instead.

  • Citi changed its online user agreement this week: customers are responsible for what third-party AI agents do with their credentials, even if the tool is hacked. Citi's own agents add no such liability
  • Nov 18 PNC changed its terms. JPMorgan and Bank of America adopted similar policies in October, and Citizens emailed customers a warning
  • US Pro ChatGPT Wallet is open to Pro subscribers in the US. It pays through the major card networks with a token in place of the card number, and every purchase needs a security check such as Face ID
  • JPMorgan blocks agents that shop with a card number a customer hands them, the WSJ reported. Its payments arm is now in Visa's Agentic Ready program, which has 140-plus members

items.title: Tencent says a new US chip rule sets China back; Jefferies sees a $44B to $62B hit to Nvidia
items.summary: Nvidia has stopped H200 sales in China, and its $130B forecast for this quarter assumes no China data center chip revenue.
items.content_html:
Nvidia has stopped H200 sales in China, and its $130B forecast for this quarter assumes no China data center chip revenue.

  • Nov 16 Commerce issued a rule so chip export limits can't be bypassed through remote access to data centers in third countries
  • Tencent president Martin Lau said the rule "sets everyone back in China" and that Tencent can no longer offer high-end GPUs, though partners elsewhere may help
  • $44–62B Jefferies' estimate of the rule's hit to next year's data center revenue; acting CEO Colette Kress says backlog means no top-line impact
  • $130B Nvidia's revenue outlook for this quarter, plus or minus 3%, assuming no data center compute revenue from China, where it has stopped selling H200 chips
